questions: Did s-bend off-track exits fall below 9 of 20 at wheel_track 0.14, compared with 9 at 0.12 and 15 at 0.10?
Did s-bend control_effort fall below 12.2, and did max_error fall below 0.047?
Did steering_oscillation stay below about 0.4 on the oval and s-bend, or did the wider track make the bends sluggish, raising max_error?
Did the oval finish rate stay at 1.0?
Did slalom line_loss_events stay at about 1.0 to 1.35, or did the wider track change the slalom result at all?
Does the controller need a different kp at 0.14 to hold the line, given that yaw per command falls as the track widens?

intent: Change one variable from the best known design (iteration 5, wheel_track 0.12, y 0.08): raise wheel_track to 0.14 m. This tests whether the narrower-track result (iteration 6, 0.10, score 496.4) continues in the other direction, reducing yaw per PWM count and making bends less overshoot-prone. Sensors stay at y 0.08, 16 mm footprints, ±0.024 m span; body, wheels and mass are unchanged. Expected: s-bend off-track exits fall below 9 of 20, s-bend control_effort falls below 12.2, oval finish stays at 1.0, and steering_oscillation stays below about 0.4. If s-bend exits rise above 9 of 20 or the oval finish falls below 0.85, revert to wheel_track 0.12 at y 0.08 as the baseline.
learning: Iteration 6 (wheel_track 0.10) showed that the narrower track is worse at y 0.08: s-bend off-track exits rose from 9 to 15 of 20 and max_error rose from 0.047 to 0.057, so the steering gain at 0.12 is already near or above the best value. Track width now has a measured gradient at y 0.08 (0.10 gives 496.4, 0.12 gives 561.6), so the 0.14 test checks whether the optimum lies above 0.12. Slalom has been 0 of 20 at every geometry tested, so track width is the only lever still open for the bends; the slalom needs a separate look only if this test fails.
rationale: Iteration 6 tested wheel_track 0.10 at y 0.08 and scored 496.4, below the 561.6 of iteration 5 at wheel_track 0.12. The narrower track made the s-bend worse: off-track exits rose from 9 to 15 of 20, max_error rose from 0.047 to 0.057, control_effort rose from 12.2 to 12.5, and oscillation rose from 0.32 to 0.32 (no change). Oval finish held at 20 of 20, and slalom stayed 0 of 20. The Integrator's entityR1 advice to keep wheel_track 0.10 was written before this race, and the race contradicts its premise, so I am not following it. The data now gives a monotone direction for track width at y 0.08: 0.10 gives 496.4 and 0.12 gives 561.6. A narrower track gives more yaw per PWM count, which here causes overshoot and off-track exits rather than helping. The natural next single-variable test is the other direction: wheel_track 0.14. This is a test of an extrapolated trend rather than a settled fact, and it contradicts my own earlier advice in this thread (I had called wheel_track 0.14 physically backwards). The race data should decide it, not the earlier theory. I will keep sensor y 0.08 (the top of the allowed range and the best lookahead), the 16 mm footprints, the ±0.024 m span, body, mass and wheels as in iteration 5. Slalom is 0 of 20 at every setting tried, so I am not chasing it with span or footprint changes here; the span widening (iteration 2) and the 12 mm footprint (iteration 0) have already been tested and did not help. Expected result: s-bend off-track exits fall below 9 of 20 and control_effort falls below 12.2, with oval finish at 1.0 and oscillation below 0.4. Risk: a wider track reduces yaw per command and may make bends sluggish, which would raise max_error. If the s-bend gets worse, the best known design is iteration 5 (wheel_track 0.12, y 0.08).
